measures.title: Grant Legislature Exclusive Authority and Prohibit Citizen-Initiated Measures on Marijuana, Narcotics, and Psychoactive Substances Amendment
measures.ballot_label: Shall Section 26, Article III of the Constitution of the State of Idaho be amended to provide that only the Idaho Legislature shall have power and authority to legalize the growing, producing, manufacturing, transporting, selling, delivering, dispensing, administering, prescribing, distributing, possessing, or using of marijuana, narcotics, or other psychoactive substances?
plain: Only the Idaho Legislature could legalize marijuana, narcotics, or other psychoactive substances.
Citizens could no longer use the ballot initiative process to legalize these substances.
The amendment does not change any current statute on its own.
measures.yes: A yes vote gives the Legislature sole power to legalize marijuana, narcotics, or other psychoactive substances.
measures.no: A no vote keeps citizens' ability to propose initiatives that would legalize or decriminalize these substances.
measures.fiscal: The official fiscal note says there is no fiscal impact except the cost of placing the measure on the ballot, which the Secretary of State estimates at no more than $200,000.

measures.title: English as Official State Language Amendment
measures.ballot_label: Shall Article X of the Constitution of the State of Idaho be amended by the addition of a new Section 8, to provide that the English language shall be the official language for the state of Idaho, and to further provide that, except as required by federal law, English shall be used in all public proceedings, public documents, ...
plain: Makes English the official language of Idaho in the state constitution (it is already the official language in statute).
Requires English in public proceedings, public documents, public instruction, and other public acts of public institutions.
Exceptions apply where federal law requires another language.
measures.yes: A yes vote adds English as the official state language to the Idaho Constitution.
measures.no: A no vote leaves English as the official language in statute only.
measures.fiscal: The official fiscal note estimates up to $300,000 for the Secretary of State to publish the voter pamphlet, a cost that occurs anyway when other measures qualify for the ballot.

measures.title: Official State Gun Advisory Question
measures.ballot_label: Which of the following guns should be designated as the state gun of Idaho? Please choose only one answer. (a) Winchester Model 1894 (.30-30); (b) Winchester Model 1873 "Gun that Won the West" (.44-40); (c) 1873 Colt Single Action Army Revolver "Peacemaker" (.45 Colt); (d) M1 Garand rifle (.30-06); ...
plain: Asks voters which of six firearms they would like as Idaho's official state gun.
It is a non-binding advisory question; the Legislature would still have to pass a law to designate a state gun.
Voters choose only one option: (a) through (f).
measures.yes: There is no yes/no choice; voters pick one of six listed guns as their preference.
measures.no: Voters may leave the question blank; the result is advisory and does not change any law.
measures.fiscal: No fiscal note is shown; the question is advisory and non-binding.

measures.title: Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act
measures.ballot_label: Measure creating right to abortion before fetus viability, and post-viability to protect health; right to privacy; healthcare provider liability protections.
plain: Creates a legal right to abortion before fetal viability, and after viability in a medical emergency that threatens the woman's life or health.
Adds a right to reproductive freedom and privacy covering decisions such as contraception, fertility treatment, miscarriage care, and prenatal and postpartum care.
Protects patients, health-care providers, and those who assist them from penalties, and requires any restriction to be justified by a compelling state interest tied to the patient's health.
measures.yes: A yes vote creates a statutory right to abortion before viability (and after in medical emergencies) with provider liability protections.
measures.no: A no vote keeps Idaho's current law, which bans abortion except to prevent the woman's death or in the first trimester for reported rape or incest.
measures.fiscal: The state estimates the initiative would increase state spending by $3,100 to $7,800 a year (under 0.001% of the state share of Medicaid) for treating complications from chemical abortions.
